description: Simergy is a graphical user interface for EnergyPlus, now offered by Digital Alchemy as a BIM-based product that lets architects, engineers, contractors and owners simulate, analyse and optimise the performance of building designs before they are built, including energy efficiency, daylighting and comfort, and assess compliance with standards such as the California building energy code. Digital Alchemy says it was developed through a public and private partnership, with workflows from early design to detailed design that support repeated analysis cycles and the exploration of HVAC system types; its guidance explains content built from library entries and templates, material layer sets and air-based HVAC systems. Search results from LBNL, Federal Labs and OSTI (secondary) describe Simergy as developed by a team led by Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, funded by DOE's Building Technologies Office, the California Energy Commission and industry partners, licensed exclusively to Digital Alchemy, with version 1.0 in July 2013 and 1.1 in April 2014. Coverage: generic. Access: a free trial download (login required); Digital Alchemy reports more than 1,300 users in more than 500 companies and 60 countries. Licence: commercial. Caveats: no current version or release date was found on the provider pages, so maintenance status is unknown. Simulation uses: EnergyPlus models for code compliance, HVAC design and daylighting studies. Related records: EnergyPlus, OpenStudio and DesignBuilder.
